subject: Post-call: Multilingual model fit + eval plan (GlobeBank)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Sousa <ana.sousa@globebank.eu>, Kenji Tanaka <k.tanaka@retailjp.co.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model fit + eval plan (GlobeBank)

Hi Ana / Kenji — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we heard about your use cases (customer support triage in FR/DE/ES and transactional summarization in JA/KO):

Summary of needs:
- High-quality understanding and generation for EU languages (French, German, Spanish) with strict PII filters and EU data residency.
- Good fallback coverage for APAC languages (Japanese, Korean) with latency constraints for Tokyo region.
- Deterministic reranking for short transactional outputs and strong hallucination mitigation for financial contexts.

Recommended model candidates to evaluate (priority order):
1) Redwood-Chat-16B (FP16) — best quality baseline for EU languages; strong safety controls and structured output support.
2) Redwood-XL-8.3B (quantized Q4) — lower cost option with very good recall on short-form prompts; recommend for high-throughput channels.
3) OpenVicuna-13B-8bit — useful as a lower-cost fallback for specific APAC-like prompt shapes; may need reinforcement on banking terminology.

Attached: locale_prompt_set_eu.zip (sample prompt sets for FR/DE/ES), and a short sample benchmark CSV (benchmark_results_sample.csv) pulled from a comparable eval run.

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): receive your priority prompt set and sample PII-redacted transcripts (you can upload to the Drive link below).
- Week 1: Redwood runs automated evals (per-language F1/ROUGE/semantic similarity + hallucination checks) and produces a baseline report.
- Week 2: manual spot-checks on highest-risk intents and a short A/B with your sample inputs in EU region.

Immediate asks for GlobeBank:
- Please confirm the list of priority languages and any strict latency SLOs for EU users.
- Can you share a redacted sample of ~200 transcripts per language (upload to the Drive link)?

Links and resources:
- Sample prompt sets: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-eval-prompts
- Benchmark view (sample): https://benchmark.redwood.ai/globebank-multilingual
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/GLB-2027-045

Next steps I suggest: we run the Week 1 automated pass and reconvene with the baseline report + recommended model pin. If that works I can schedule a follow-up next-Tuesday for a 30m review.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa — thanks for the recap and clear plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Languages and priority:
- Priority 1: French (fr-FR) and German (de-DE) for the support triage flow.
- Priority 2: Spanish (es-ES) for knowledge-base summarization.
- APAC (Japanese, Korean) are lower priority but we would like baseline coverage.

2) Data residency / compliance:
- All sample transcripts we share must be stored and processed within the EU for the eval runs used against EU data. Can you confirm Redwood will use EU-hosted inference for those runs? We discussed private deployment earlier — if needed we can scope Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1.

3) Benchmarks and regressions:
- Can you share the exact scoring definitions you will use for hallucination/regression detection? We want to be able to reproduce the checks on our side.

4) Timeline constraint:
- We need the Week 1 automated pass completed by COB next Friday (May 14) to sync with our internal stakeholders. Is that feasible?

Appreciate the attachments — I'll prep redacted samples (we may need a small addendum to the NDA before sharing). Also looping in our Tokyo contact (Kenji) to ask if he can provide a couple of JA/KO samples for the fallback eval.

Thanks,
Ana

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Sousa <ana.sousa@globebank.eu>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 01:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model fit + eval plan (GlobeBank)

Hi Ana — welcome, and thanks Marissa. Quick note on the technical plan and compliance items you raised: 

EU hosting / residency:
- We can run all EU-facing evals in our eu-west-1 region (Redwood Dedicated or Hosted EU cluster) and ensure logs/artifacts remain in-region. For production, Dedicated capacity or Private deployment are available options; I'll include a short ng-ops checklist in the attached eval plan.

Scoring definitions (high-level):
- Semantic Accuracy: sentence-level embedding similarity (cosine) against human reference; threshold buckets (>=0.85 good, 0.70-0.85 caution, <0.70 flagged).
- Hallucination Rate: percent of model outputs with fabricated facts per a 100-sample manual spot-check (binary label).
- Slot/Entity Extraction F1: for transactional intents where structured fields must be preserved.
- Latency P95: measured in eu-west-1 / ap-northeast-1 for per-token and end-to-end.

Deliverables and timeline (confirmed):
- Tue (May 11): we receive your redacted sample uploads + confirmation of priority languages.
- Thu (May 13): automated eval pass complete; we post the baseline CSV and short summary.
- Fri COB (May 14): manual spot-checks + recommendations deck.

I've attached the eval plan (eval_plan_globebank_20270510.pdf) which outlines sample sizes, scoring scripts we'll run, and the secure upload instructions. If you need the scoring scripts to reproduce locally, we can share a reproducible notebook and a small docker image after the NDA addendum.

Next steps from Redwood: I'll queue the automated runs as soon as the samples are uploaded to the Drive link and will ping when the baseline draft is ready. Marissa — if you can lock the 30m review on May 18 or 19 that would work for the team.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
